booting.text: FX desk — give me a moment, the board is still warming up.

no_account.text: Dollars for euros or shekels? I'd love to, but I trade out of your account, not out of my pocket. Ines opens one at Account Opening.

why_account.text: Every trade here is executed by your own account contract, on the exchange's terms and under your guard list. Until that contract exists there is nothing for the router to talk to.

desk_closed.text: Board's dark today — the branch can't reach the exchange floor. Counter and the vault are unaffected.

why_desk_closed.text: {fx_chain_note} When that side isn't configured or won't answer, I close the board rather than quote you a price I can't honour.

no_till.text: You've no till on the exchange floor yet. I can open one — {fx_till_note}.

choices.working: Opening your till and registering the exchange door…

why_till.text: Your FX till is {fx_till_note}. Same owner, same tellers, same rules — and either way the exchange itself is on Sepolia, because that is where the pools are.

closed_door.text: Till's there, but the exchange door isn't on your approved list yet. Three doors, three keys — I can't trade until the manager's list says so.

choices.working: Registering three functions and three addresses…

opened.text: Done. Your account may now call exactly three things: the dollar's approve, Permit2's approve, and the exchange router's execute. Nothing else — not the euro, not the shekel; those only ever come *in*. {fx_usdc} {fx_symbol_in} in the till.

swapped.text: Filled. {fx_amount_in} {fx_symbol_in} went out, {fx_symbol_out} came back — the till holds {fx_usdc} {fx_symbol_in}, {fx_eur} EUR and {fx_ils} ILS now. Receipt's on the board.

whitelist.text: Three, and only three: approve on the dollar, approve on Permit2, execute on the exchange router. That list is on your account, not on my desk — I couldn't send your money anywhere else if you asked me to. And it's one-way: I sell euros and shekels for dollars; I don't buy them back, so your account never approves either of them.

why_swap.text: Your account calls the exchange router directly, but only because that router is on your approved list for that exact function. Same guard as payments. Euros and shekels are two pools behind one door.

why_guard.text: GuardController holds a whitelist per function selector. Your till registered three schemas — approve(address,uint256), Permit2's approve, and execute(bytes,bytes[],uint256) — and whitelisted one address for each. You sign a meta-transaction, the FX teller submits it, and the account refuses any target that is not on that list. A swap is a treasury operation here, not a wallet pop-up.

why_quote.text: The board is the exchange's own quoter, asked off-chain — it costs nothing and signs nothing. Each currency has its own pool, a hundred million deep, so a desk-sized order barely moves the rate. I take one percent off the quote as your floor, stamp a five-minute deadline, and the router refuses the trade if the pool has moved past that floor by the time it lands.
